rules: Only checks that move conversion during a sale and can be measured from the outside now.

A pop-up with a signup form and a pop-up without a form are separate things: capture checks (blocks E-K) count only signup forms; pop-ups without a form are listed in block L and never mixed into capture counts.
A pop-up covering the screen or the product page is not a finding by itself: that is what a pop-up is for.
Every verdict names its evidence: a screenshot file, or a value from walk.json.

statuses.partial: present but weak or incomplete; the evidence says what is missing
statuses.missing: would be visible on a page the walk reached, and is not there
statuses.cannot_verify: depends on something the walk could not see; the evidence says what would be needed
statuses.info: a fact to report, not a pass/fail (mechanics, pop-ups without a form)

items.title: The sale is announced in the first screen of the homepage
items.what: An announcement bar, hero or banner states the sale before any scroll, on desktop and on mobile.
items.how: Homepage above-the-fold screenshots (popups closed), both devices; walk.json home.page_facts.announcement_bars, top_strip_text, hero.
items.read: done = visible on both devices; partial = one device only or below the fold; missing = no sale message on the first screen.
items.why: Shoppers arriving in sale week decide in seconds whether the sale is on here; if the first screen does not say so, many leave to a store that does.

items.title: The offer is concrete
items.what: The sale message names a number: % off, $ off, a price, or a clear gift threshold.
items.how: Same screenshots as A1 and home.page_facts.text_signals.percent_off.
items.read: done = a number is stated; partial = only 'sale' / 'deals' with no number; not_applicable if A1 is missing.
items.why: A number lets the shopper judge the deal at once; 'big sale' gives nothing to compare.

items.title: The sale shows when it ends
items.what: An end date or a countdown tied to the real end of the sale is visible on the homepage or sale pages.
items.how: Screenshots; walk.json home.live_timers (text that changed between two reads = a running timer).
items.read: done = date or running timer; missing = no end shown while a sale is announced; not_applicable if no sale is announced.
items.why: A real deadline is the honest reason to buy now instead of later.

items.title: One click from the menu to the sale
items.what: The main navigation has a sale / Black Friday / deals entry that leads to the discounted products.
items.how: Header screenshots and home.page_facts.header.links.
items.read: done = a sale link in the main menu (desktop, and in the mobile menu when visible); missing = sale reachable only through banners or not at all.
items.why: Shoppers who came for the sale look for it in the menu; a hidden sale page loses them.

items.title: Free-shipping threshold is stated site-wide
items.what: The free-shipping condition (or 'free shipping') is visible on every page, usually in the top bar.
items.how: Top-bar screenshots; text_signals.free_shipping on home and product pages.
items.read: done = threshold or free shipping shown site-wide; missing = only in the cart or nowhere; not_applicable = store never ships free.
items.why: Shipping cost is the most common reason for abandoned carts; knowing the threshold early raises basket size.

items.title: Holiday delivery cutoff is shown
items.what: A last-order date for delivery before the holidays, or a delivery promise for the season.
items.how: Screenshots of home, product, cart, FAQ; text_signals.shipping_cutoff.
items.read: done = a cutoff or delivery-by date is visible; missing = none; cannot_verify outside the holiday season.
items.why: Gift buyers stop buying when they are unsure the parcel arrives in time.

items.title: Sale price next to the original price on product tiles
items.what: Discounted products show the old price struck through, or a % badge, on category tiles.
items.how: Category page screenshots; category.page_facts.product_tiles[].strike_price.
items.read: done = discounted tiles show both prices; missing = only one price while the sale is on; not_applicable = no discounted products found.
items.why: The saving is the reason to click during a sale; a tile with one price hides it.

items.title: The product page shows the saving
items.what: Old and new price (or % off) next to the buy button on a discounted product.
items.how: Product page screenshots, both devices.
items.read: done = visible near the price; missing = discounted product with one price; not_applicable = the product walked is not discounted.
items.why: The decision is made at the buy button; the saving must be there.

items.title: Reviews near the price
items.what: Star rating and review count on the product page above the fold, and ideally on tiles.
items.how: Product and category screenshots; page_facts.apps (review apps) and product_tiles[].rating.
items.read: done = rating with count on the product page above the fold; partial = only lower on the page or only on tiles; missing = none.
items.why: First-time sale shoppers rely on other buyers' ratings when they do not know the brand.

items.title: Delivery and returns at the buy button
items.what: Delivery time or date and the returns promise are visible near the add-to-cart button.
items.how: Product page screenshots; product text_signals.delivery_estimate, returns.
items.read: done = both; partial = one of them; missing = neither.
items.why: Doubts about delivery and returns stop the click at the last step.

items.title: Add to cart is in the first screen on mobile
items.what: On a phone, the add-to-cart button is visible without scrolling, or a sticky add-to-cart appears.
items.how: Mobile product page screenshots (top and second screen).
items.read: done = visible in the first screen or sticky; missing = only after scrolling with no sticky button.
items.why: Most sale traffic is on phones; a buy button below the fold costs taps and buyers.

items.title: The cart shows the total saving
items.what: The cart states how much the shopper saves (old price struck through or a 'You save' line).
items.how: Cart screenshots (page or drawer), both devices; cart page text.
items.read: done = saving visible; missing = discounted item in the cart with no saving shown; not_applicable = the item added was not discounted.
items.why: Seeing the saving again at the cart confirms the decision and lowers abandonment.

items.title: Progress to free shipping in the cart
items.what: A bar or line 'X away from free shipping' in the cart.
items.how: Cart screenshots; cart text.
items.read: done = progress shown; missing = threshold exists (A5) but the cart does not show the gap; not_applicable = no threshold.
items.why: A visible gap to free shipping makes shoppers add an item instead of leaving.

items.title: Express checkout from the cart
items.what: Wallet buttons (Shop Pay, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal) in the cart, not only at checkout.
items.how: Cart screenshots; cart.checkout_view.express_buttons.
items.read: done = at least one wallet button in the cart; missing = none.
items.why: Wallets skip the form, which matters most on phones in a busy week.

items.title: A relevant add-on in the cart
items.what: A recommendation or bundle offer in the cart.
items.how: Cart screenshots.
items.read: done = a recommendation with an add button; missing = none.
items.why: Shoppers in a buying mood accept a small add-on; it lifts order value.

items.title: Guest checkout is the default
items.what: Checkout opens on contact and delivery fields; signing in is optional.
items.how: Checkout screenshots; checkout.login_prompt and fields.
items.read: done = no forced account; missing = an account is required; cannot_verify if checkout did not load.
items.why: A forced account is one of the top reasons buyers abandon checkout.

items.title: Wallet buttons above the form at checkout
items.what: Express checkout buttons are the first thing on the checkout page.
items.how: Checkout screenshots; checkout.express_buttons.
items.read: done = wallets above the form; partial = present but below the form; missing = none.
items.why: Shoppers with a wallet finish in seconds; the rest of the form becomes optional.

items.title: Reassurance near the pay button
items.what: Secure payment, returns or guarantee text near the final button.
items.how: Checkout full-page screenshot; checkout text.
items.read: done = present; missing = none.
items.why: The last doubt appears right before paying.

items.title: Marketing consent at checkout is optional and unticked
items.what: An email/SMS marketing checkbox exists at checkout and is not pre-ticked.
items.how: checkout.checkboxes (label, checked).
items.read: done = present and unticked; partial = present and pre-ticked (consent issue in the EU); missing = no marketing opt-in at checkout.
items.why: Checkout is the cheapest place to win a subscriber; a pre-ticked box is not valid consent in the EU.

items.title: Signup form for a new visitor on the homepage
items.what: A pop-up with an email or phone field appears for a first-time visitor on the homepage.
items.how: Scenario home_new, both devices: overlays of kind capture_form.
items.read: done = on both devices; partial = one device; missing = none.
items.why: Sale traffic peaks this week; visitors who leave without a contact cannot be brought back.

items.title: Signup form for a visitor landing on a product page
items.what: A visitor who arrives straight on a product page (an ad click) gets a signup form.
items.how: Scenario product_land, both devices.
items.read: done = on both devices; partial = one device; missing = none while the homepage has one (E1).
items.why: Paid traffic lands on products, not on the homepage; a homepage-only form misses it.

items.title: Browse abandonment
items.what: After viewing three products without adding to cart, an exit attempt shows a signup form.
items.how: Scenario browse_exit: popups closed on each product page, exit intent on the third.
items.read: done = a form appears after the exit attempt; missing = nothing appears.
items.why: A visitor who browsed several products is interested; leaving without a contact loses the warmest lead.

items.title: Cart abandonment with a full cart
items.what: An exit attempt with a product in the cart shows a form or an offer.
items.how: Scenario exit_cart: product added, exit intent on the homepage.
items.read: done = a form appears; missing = nothing appears.
items.why: Shoppers with a full cart who leave are the closest to buying.

items.title: The exit offer differs from the welcome offer
items.what: The form shown on exit is a different form or offer from the one shown on arrival.
items.how: Compare form text of home_new with exit_cart / browse_exit forms.
items.read: done = different; partial = the same form reappears on exit; not_applicable = no exit form.
items.why: A visitor who already closed the welcome form will close it again; exit needs its own reason.

items.title: The offer changes with what the visitor does
items.what: Different forms or offers by page type (home, product, cart, exit).
items.how: Distinct signup-form texts across scenarios.
items.read: done = more than one distinct form; missing = one form for every situation; not_applicable = fewer than one form.
items.why: A product viewer and a homepage visitor want different things; one offer fits neither well.

items.title: A returning visitor is treated differently
items.what: The same visitor coming back (same browser) sees a different form, a teaser, or nothing, instead of the same form again.
items.how: Scenario return_visit after home_new with popups closed.
items.read: done = different form or nothing; partial = the same form again; not_applicable = no form in E1.
items.why: Showing the same closed form again annoys returning shoppers who came back to buy.

items.title: Subscribers do not see the signup form again
items.what: After signing up, the next visit shows no signup form.
items.how: Test signup (block J), then a new visit with the same browser storage.
items.read: done = no form after signup; missing = the form shows again; cannot_verify = the test signup was not run.
items.why: Asking a subscriber to subscribe wastes the screen that could sell.

items.title: No discount pop-up in cart or checkout
items.what: A signup pop-up with a discount does not open on the cart or checkout pages.
items.how: Overlays seen in the cart and checkout scenarios.
items.read: done = none there; missing = a discount form opens in the cart or at checkout.
items.why: A shopper in the cart has already chosen; a discount there only cuts margin and distracts from paying.

items.title: A teaser stays after the form is closed
items.what: After closing the form, a small tab or button lets the visitor reopen it on the next page.
items.how: home_new: teaser after close and on the next page.
items.read: done = teaser visible; missing = the form is gone for good after one close; not_applicable = no form.
items.why: Many close the form by reflex and want the offer later, at the cart.

items.title: The form is not covered by another layer
items.what: The signup form does not appear at the same time as the cookie banner or another pop-up.
items.how: overlap events in the first seconds of every scenario.
items.read: done = no overlap; missing = the form shares the screen with another blocking layer.
items.why: Two layers at once: the visitor closes both, and the form never gets read.

items.title: What the signup form offers
items.what: Offer type and depth: % off, $ off, free shipping, gift, early access, or nothing.
items.how: Text of the signup forms seen.
items.read: info, with the type and the deepest number found.
items.why: The offer is the main lever of the form's conversion.

items.title: The form does not offer less than the site sale
items.what: The form's discount is not smaller than the discount already advertised on the site.
items.how: Deepest % in the signup forms vs deepest % in the homepage sale text.
items.read: done = form offer >= site sale, or an exclusive non-discount reason (early access, extra gift); missing = the form offers less than the open sale (e.g. 10% vs 30%); not_applicable = no sale or no form.
items.why: During a 30% sale a 10% signup offer gives no reason to subscribe.

items.title: The form speaks about the sale
items.what: The signup form mentions Black Friday / Cyber Monday / the holiday sale or early access.
items.how: Signup form text.
items.read: done = sale wording; missing = an evergreen form during the sale; not_applicable = no form.
items.why: A form tied to the sale ('get early access') converts better in sale week than a generic newsletter ask.

items.title: Multi-step form
items.what: Email (or a question) first, more fields on a next step.
items.how: Signup form steps seen.
items.read: info: yes / no.
items.why: Asking for less on the first step lowers the effort to start.

items.title: Collects phone numbers
items.what: A phone field in a signup form.
items.how: Signup form inputs.
items.read: info: yes / no.
items.why: SMS is a second channel for the sale week; a phone field on the first step lowers signups.

items.title: Quiz or choice
items.what: A question with choices before the contact field.
items.how: Signup form text and buttons.
items.read: info: yes / no.
items.why: A choice first engages the visitor and lets the offer match the answer.

items.title: Game
items.what: Spin-to-win, scratch card or similar.
items.how: Signup form text.
items.read: info: yes / no.
items.why: Games raise signups when the prizes are equal in value to a plain offer.

items.title: Countdown in the form
items.what: A timer inside the signup form.
items.how: Signup form text.
items.read: info: yes / no.
items.why: Only credible when tied to the real sale end.

items.title: The thank-you step gives the code
items.what: After submitting the email, the form shows the code or says where it is.
items.how: signup_test.py: text after submit.
items.read: done = code shown; partial = 'check your email' only; missing = no confirmation; cannot_verify = test not run.
items.why: A shopper ready to buy now wants the code now, not in an inbox.

items.title: Consent text under the email/phone field
items.what: Privacy / unsubscribe / SMS terms text next to the fields.
items.how: signup_test.py: text near the inputs.
items.read: done = present; missing = none; cannot_verify = no form reached.
items.why: SMS and email consent text is a legal requirement in the US (TCPA) and the EU (GDPR).

items.title: The welcome email arrives
items.what: A welcome email with the promised code arrives, and how fast.
items.how: The tester's inbox after the test signup.
items.read: done = arrives within 5 minutes with the code; partial = later or without the code; missing = nothing in 30 minutes; cannot_verify = no inbox access.
items.why: The first email is opened most; a late or empty one wastes the signup.

items.title: The code works in the cart
items.what: The code from the form or email applies a discount in the cart.
items.how: signup_test.py --code: Shopify /discount/<code>, then the cart.
items.read: done = discount applied; missing = rejected; cannot_verify = no code or not Shopify.
items.why: A code that fails at checkout turns a buyer into a complaint.

items.title: The form fits a phone screen
items.what: Content inside the screen, close button at least 24 px, field font at least 16 px, main button visible.
items.how: mobile_check.js on every mobile signup form.
items.read: done = all four hold; partial = one fails; missing = two or more fail; not_applicable = no mobile form.
items.why: A form that overflows or zooms on tap loses mobile signups.

items.title: The keyboard leaves the field visible
items.what: The email field sits high enough that the phone keyboard (about 45% of the screen) does not cover it.
items.how: Field position in the mobile form.
items.read: done = field bottom above 55% of screen height; missing = lower; not_applicable = no mobile form.
items.why: A field hidden under the keyboard makes typing blind.

items.title: Pop-ups without a form
items.what: Announcement or promo pop-ups with no contact field: what they say and where.
items.how: Overlays of kind other_overlay / vendor_overlay without inputs.
items.read: info.
items.why: Listed apart so they never count as capture.

items.title: The signup form is translated
items.what: If the site has another language version, the form there is in that language.
items.how: hreflang alternates: one other language, homepage, form text.
items.read: done = translated; missing = the form stays in English; not_applicable = one language only.
items.why: A form in the wrong language converts poorly with the visitors that version exists for.

items.title: Delivery times for the sale are answered
items.what: FAQ or shipping page answers delivery times in the busy season.
items.how: FAQ/help page screenshots and text.
items.read: done = answered; missing = no FAQ answer about delivery times; cannot_verify = no FAQ page found.
items.why: Unanswered delivery questions become support tickets or lost orders.

items.title: Returns policy is easy to find
items.what: A returns link in the footer or menu and the window stated.
items.how: Footer screenshot and links; FAQ page.
items.read: done = link and window; partial = link only; missing = none.
items.why: Gift buyers check returns before paying.

items.title: Payment methods are shown
items.what: Payment icons in the footer or near the buy button.
items.how: Footer screenshots; page_facts.payment_icons.
items.read: done = shown; missing = none.
items.why: Seeing a familiar way to pay reassures first-time buyers.

items.title: A way to reach the store
items.what: Chat, email or phone visible on the site.
items.how: Screenshots; page_facts.apps (chat apps), footer.phone.
items.read: done = visible; missing = none.
items.why: Questions in sale week need an answer before the deal ends.

items.title: The homepage loads fast on a phone
items.what: Largest Contentful Paint of the mobile homepage, one lab run.
items.how: PerformanceObserver largest-contentful-paint in the mobile home scenario.
items.read: done = under 2.5 s; partial = 2.5-4 s; missing = over 4 s. One run on the auditor's connection, so treat as indicative.
items.why: Sale traffic spikes slow sites down; each second of delay loses mobile buyers.
